key_insight: The paper introduces two conformal methods that can screen for AI-generated text within a document while still controlling false alerts at finite sample sizes. The key advance is adaptive prefix-based screening: the system can choose how much of a document to inspect and still provide valid error control.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of detecting AI-generated text in documents without over-flagging human-written content, especially when inspection must be adaptive and may stop early before reading the full document.
method: Uses document-level exchangeability between human calibration documents and a new null document to guarantee finite-sample validity.
Allows adaptive selection of document prefixes and detectors based on observed evidence, rather than requiring a fixed full-document scan.
Presents two conformal constructions that control false-alert rates even when token-level dependencies within a document are unrestricted.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it provides a principled way to screen documents for AI-generated text with reliable error control, even under realistic, variable-length inspection budgets. It is especially useful for moderation, auditing, and evaluation pipelines where false positives are costly.

paper_title: Two Conformal Constructions for Adaptive Within-Document AI-Text Screening
paper_authors: Marco Mandap, Jerahmeel Hipolito, Arcel Galvez, Charlie Margaret Balagtas, Michael Joshua Buluran
